'''Baylor Arthur Scheierman''' (born September 26, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref name="NBAProfile">{{cite web |title=Baylor Scheierman |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1631248/baylor-scheierman |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> He played [[college basketball]] for the [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State Jackrabbits]] and the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]].

==High school career==
Scheierman attended Aurora High School in [[Aurora, Nebraska]], where he competed in basketball, football, baseball, golf, and his favorite sport Gaelic football.<ref name="Zimmer">{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Zimmer |title=Baylor Scheierman uses football skills to lead South Dakota State's high-powered hoops offense |url=https://www.argusleader.com/story/sports/college/south-dakota-state-university/2022/01/22/baylor-scheierman-south-dakota-state-jackrabbits-football-skills-basketball-offense-summit-league/6579144001/ |work=[[Argus Leader]] |date=January 22, 2022 |access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 16.1 points, six rebounds and six assists per game.<ref name="SDSUSigning">{{cite press release |title=Men's Basketball announces four signees Wednesday |url=https://gojacks.com/news/2018/11/14/mens-basketball-announces-four-signees-wednesday |publisher=South Dakota State University Athletics |date=November 14, 2018 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> He averaged 22.1 points, 9.8 rebounds and 6.5 assists per game as a senior and helped Aurora reach the state basketball tournament.<ref name="Zimmer"/>

As Aurora's quarterback, Scheierman threw for 3,942 yards and a then-state-record 59 touchdowns during his senior season, leading the school to the Nebraska Class C-1 state championship.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gene |last=Schinzel |title=Aurora grad Baylor Scheierman is making a big impact for South Dakota State |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/aurora-grad-baylor-scheierman-is-making-a-big-impact-for-south-dakota-state/article_af83a156-4197-11eb-812e-df1efe56d3fb.html |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=December 19, 2020 |access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref><ref name="CreightonBio">{{cite web |title=Baylor Scheierman |url=https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/baylor-scheierman/7816 |website=Creighton University Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> He committed to play college basketball for South Dakota State in November 2017.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mike |last=Sautter |title=Aurora guard Baylor Scheierman commits to South Dakota State |url=https://omaha.com/sports/high-school/recruiting/aurora-guard-baylor-scheierman-commits-to-south-dakota-state/article_0cd8ef98-c8ef-11e7-8398-6f06e31198fd.html |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=November 13, 2017 |access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at South Dakota State, Scheierman averaged 6.0 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game. He increased his averages to 15.4 points, 9.2 rebounds and 4.0 assists as a sophomore and was named first-team All-[[Summit League]].<ref name="CreightonBio"/><ref>{{cite press release |title=Oral Roberts' Abmas collects #SummitMBB Player of the Year honors |url=https://thesummitleague.org/news/2021/3/3/awards-oral-roberts-abmas-collects-summitmbb-player-of-the-year-honors.aspx |publisher=[[Summit League]] |date=March 4, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref> During his junior season, he averaged 16.2 points, 7.8 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game, led the conference in both rebounds and assists, and was named the [[Summit League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Summit League Player of the Year]].<ref name="SummitAwards">{{cite press release |title=SDSU's Scheierman tabbed #SummitMBB Player of the Year |url=https://thesummitleague.org/news/2022/3/3/awards-sdsus-scheierman-garners-summitmbb-player-of-the-year-award.aspx |publisher=[[Summit League]] |date=March 3, 2022 |access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref>

Following his junior season, Scheierman entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]] and declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Zimmer |title=Baylor Scheierman declares for 2022 NBA Draft |url=https://www.argusleader.com/story/sports/college/south-dakota-state-university/2022/03/24/baylor-scheierman-declares-2022-nba-draft/7160503001/ |work=[[Argus Leader]] |date=March 24, 2022 |access-date=March 25, 2022}}</ref> On May 3, 2022, he committed to [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] while remaining in the draft.<ref>{{cite web |first=Joe |last=Tipton |title=South Dakota St. transfer Baylor Scheierman commits to Creighton |url=https://www.on3.com/news/south-dakota-st-transfer-baylor-scheierman-commits-to-creighton/ |website=On3 |date=May 3, 2022 |access-date=May 3, 2022}}</ref> He withdrew from the draft on May 24.<ref>{{cite news |title=Creighton transfer guard Baylor Scheierman withdraws from NBA Draft: Reports |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3490781/2022/05/24/creighton-transfer-guard-baylor-scheierman-withdraws-from-nba-draft/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=May 24, 2022 |access-date=May 24, 2022}}</ref>

In his first season at Creighton, Scheierman averaged 12.8 points, 8.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game, received honorable-mention All-[[Big East]] recognition and helped the Bluejays reach the Elite Eight of the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].<ref name="CreightonBio"/> He returned for his final season of eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |first=Nick |last=Revia |title=Baylor Scheierman returning to Creighton for the final year of eligibility |url=https://fox42kptm.com/sports/content/baylor-scheierman-returning-to-creighton-for-final-year-of-eligibility |work=KPTM |date=April 13, 2023 |access-date=March 14, 2024}}</ref> During the 2023–24 season, Scheierman averaged 18.5 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. He became the first Creighton player to record a [[triple-double]] in points, rebounds and assists when he had 15 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists against [[2023–24 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]], and he helped Creighton advance to the Sweet Sixteen of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].<ref name="CreightonBio"/> He was a unanimous first-team All-Big East selection and received third-team All-America honors from the Associated Press, USBWA, NABC and ''The Sporting News''.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Associated Press 2023-24 men's college basketball All-America teams |url=https://apnews.com/article/ap-all-america-mens-basketball-team-42313363c91cbee1bec7d23c79dc0afa |work=AP News |date=March 19, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |title=USBWA unveils 2023-24 Men's All-America Team |url=https://usbwa.com/usbwa/news/2024/03/20/usbwa-unveils-2023-24-mens-all-america-team |publisher=United States Basketball Writers Association |date=March 20, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |title=NABC Announces Division I All-America Honors |url=https://nabc.com/nabc_releases/2024/nabc-announces-division-i-all-america-honors/ |publisher=National Association of Basketball Coaches |date=March 20, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Mike |last=DeCourcy |title=The Sporting News 2023-24 College Basketball All-America Team |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/sporting-news-2023-24-college-basketball-all-america-team/e26e418e473ad42c43e50097 |work=[[The Sporting News]] |date=March 12, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Scheierman was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 30th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] on June 26, 2024.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Celtics Select Scheierman and Watson in 2024 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease-20240627-celtics-select-sscheierman-and-watson-in-2024-nba-draft |publisher=Boston Celtics |date=June 27, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> He signed with the Celtics on July 6.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Boston Celtics Sign Scheierman |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20240706-boston-celtics-sign-scheierman |publisher=Boston Celtics |date=July 6, 2024 |access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref> Scheierman made his NBA debut against the [[Washington Wizards]] on October 24, scoring four points and recording one rebound in eight minutes.<ref name="MaineAssignment">{{cite news |first=Spencer |last=Martin |title=Boston First Round Pick Baylor Scheierman Assigned to Maine Celtics |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/scheierman-11052024 |work=Maine Celtics |date=November 5, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> During his rookie season, Boston assigned him to its [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Maine Celtics]], eight times between November 5, 2024, and February 3, 2025.<ref name="MaineAssignment"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Boston Celtics G League Assignments and Call Ups |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Boston-Celtics/2/gleague-transactions |website=RealGM |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>

On March 18, 2025, Scheierman scored a then-career-high 20 points and made six three-pointers in a 104–96 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Baylor Scheierman's big night boosts Celtics past Nets |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/baylor-scheiermans-big-night-boosts-celtics-past-nets--flm-2025-03-19/ |work=Reuters |agency=Field Level Media |date=March 19, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> He made his first NBA start on April 9 against the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Baylor Scheierman 2024-25 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/scheiba01/gamelog/2025 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> He finished his rookie season having appeared in 31 games, including two starts, and averaged 3.6 points per game.<ref name="BRef">{{cite web |title=Baylor Scheierman Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/scheiba01.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>

On October 30, 2025, the Celtics exercised Scheierman's team option for the [[2026–27 NBA season|2026–27 season]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Darren |last=Hartwell |title=Celtics exercise team option Baylor Scheierman for 2026-27 season: Report |url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/baylor-scheierman-contract-team-option/743301/ |work=NBC Sports Boston |date=October 30, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref> During his second NBA season, he appeared in 77 games, made 20 starts and averaged 5.5 points and 3.5 rebounds while shooting 39.9 percent from three-point range.<ref name="BRef"/> On April 12, 2026, Scheierman scored a career-high 30 points and added seven rebounds and seven assists in a 113–108 victory over the Magic in Boston's final regular-season game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Baylor Scheierman, Celtics top Magic, enter playoffs on winning note |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/baylor-scheierman-celtics-top-magic-enter-playoffs-winning-note--flm-2026-04-13/ |work=Reuters |agency=Field Level Media |date=April 13, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>
